title: Allergenic fungal spores and pollen (illustrative starter list)
description: Fungi whose spores, and plants whose pollen, are recognised sources of airborne allergens. Pollen is usually only resolved to genus or family by sequence. Read counts reflect DNA, not spore or pollen counts. Taxonomy IDs were written from knowledge of NCBI Taxonomy and could not all be checked against it when the list was made; screening ignores an ID whose name in your taxonomy belongs to a different genus, and reports it under list_validation_warnings.

entries.name: Alternaria
entries.notes: Major outdoor spore allergen, peaks in late summer; associated with asthma.

entries.name: Cladosporium
entries.notes: Usually the most abundant airborne spore outdoors.

entries.name: Aspergillus
entries.notes: Allergenic; A. fumigatus is also an opportunistic pathogen (see human pathogens).

entries.name: Fusarium
entries.notes: Some species allergenic; several are plant pathogens.

entries.name: Ganoderma
entries.notes: Bracket fungus; basidiospores are allergenic in some regions.

entries.name: Poaceae
entries.notes: Grass pollen: the most common pollen allergy in the UK and Europe.

entries.name: Betula
entries.notes: Birch: major tree pollen allergen in spring.

entries.name: Alnus
entries.notes: Alder: early spring; cross-reacts with birch.

entries.name: Corylus
entries.notes: Hazel: late winter to early spring; cross-reacts with birch.

entries.name: Olea
entries.notes: Olive: major allergen in Mediterranean regions.

entries.name: Cupressaceae
entries.notes: Cypress family: allergenic in southern Europe.

entries.name: Ambrosia
entries.notes: Ragweed: potent allergen; invasive in parts of Europe.
